messages.subject: plot with error-bars and upperlimits
parts:
Hi,

I started using ggplot recently and find it amazing.

I have a table with x, y, y-error.
I wish to plot the points with error-bars on y, except that if the y-
error equals a fixed large value (say 99.0) I want to show it as an
upper-limit (using another color or symbol for that row, or a one
sided error-bar). An example is shown at this URL:
http://nesssi.cacr.caltech.edu/catalina/20101019/1010190150134113452p.html

If I have the following snippet of a table, how do I do it with
ggplot2?

2454938.875 21.27 99.00
2454938.887 20.05 0.15
2454938.898 20.20 0.18
2454938.909 21.11 99.00
2454938.922 21.01 99.00
2454938.932 21.07 99.00
2454938.945 20.68 0.24

Here is what I do up to the error-part bit:

X <- read.table('mydata')
qplot(V1,V2,data=X,ylim=c(max(X$V2),min(X$V2))) +
geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=V2+V3,ymax=V2-V3),width=0.1)

or

qplot(V1,V2,data=X) + coord_cartesian(ylim=c(max(X$V2),min(X$V2))) +
geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=V2-V3,ymax=V2+V3))

BTW, is there any better way to invert the y-axis than what I am
doing? My first method will tend to not plot the error bars on the two
extreme points in y.

Thanks!
-ashish

> 2454938.887    20.05     0.15
> 2454938.898    20.20     0.18
> 2454938.909    21.11    99.00
> 2454938.922    21.01    99.00
> 2454938.932    21.07    99.00
> 2454938.945    20.68      0.24
>
> Here is what I do up to the error-part bit:
>
> X <- read.table('mydata')
> qplot(V1,V2,data=X,ylim=c(max(X$V2),min(X$V2))) +
> geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=V2+V3,ymax=V2-V3),width=0.1)
>
> or
>
> qplot(V1,V2,data=X) + coord_cartesian(ylim=c(max(X$V2),min(X$V2))) +
> geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=V2-V3,ymax=V2+V3))

Create an indicator variable for which type of plotting you want, and
then subset the data on that variable for each plot type, At the same
time, use that variable in the colour and shape aesthetic. I manually
set the colors and hid the legends. Setting the ymax to Inf will draw
out to the extreme of the graph without extending the scale.
scale_y_reverse inverts the axis (without having to know the limits).

X <-
structure(list(V1 = c(2454938.875, 2454938.887, 2454938.898,
2454938.909, 2454938.922, 2454938.932, 2454938.945), V2 = c(21.27,
20.05, 20.2, 21.11, 21.01, 21.07, 20.68), V3 = c(99, 0.15, 0.18,
99, 99, 99, 0.24)), .Names = c("V1", "V2", "V3"), class =
"data.frame", row.names = c(NA,
-7L))


X <- transform(X, limit=(V3==99))

ggplot(X, aes(x=V1, y=V2, colour=limit, shape=limit)) +
geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=V2+V3,ymax=V2-V3),width=0.1, data=X[!X$limit,])
+
geom_point(data=X[!X$limit,]) +
geom_pointrange(aes(ymin=V2, ymax=Inf), data=X[X$limit,]) +
scale_y_reverse() +
scale_colour_manual(values=c("blue","red"), legend=FALSE) +
scale_shape(legend=FALSE)

> BTW, is there any better way to invert the y-axis than what I am
> doing? My first method will tend to not plot the error bars on the two
> extreme points in y.

That's because using ylim tells ggplot to throw out any points/data
outside that range, so the upper error bars get tossed out.

> Thanks!
> -ashish
